newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN WINS GIANT SLALOM WORLD TITLE.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-VON GRUENIGEN WINS GIANT SLALOM WORLD TITLE.

text.p: Switzerland's Michael Von Gruenigen won the giant slalom at the Alpine skiing championships on Wednesday for his first world gold medal.

The World Cup giant slalom champion, who took bronze in slalom and giant at the 1996 championships, clocked a combined time over the two legs of two minutes 48.23 seconds to dethrone Alberto Tomba, who failed to finish the first leg.
Norwegian all-rounder Lasse Kjus picked up his third silver medal of the championships after finishing second in the super-G and downhill. His time was 2:49.35.
Andreas Schifferer was the surprise third finisher, collecting Austria's third bronze in 2:49.68 to edge Swiss Steve Locher out of the medals by 0.03 seconds.
It was Switzerland's second gold of the championships, following Bruno Kernen's men's downhill win.
Before that, the Swiss had not won a world title since 1993. Pirmin Zurbriggen was the last Swiss man to win the giant slalom title, at home in Crans Montana 10 years ago.
Tomba, the big hope of the home crowd, went out in the first leg after barely one minute on the icy Sises 2 piste.

The defending champion, starting 16th after last month losing his place in the top 15 seeds for the first time in a decade, lost his balance at the top of the piste, recovered and then got into even greater trouble before skiing to a halt at the side of the course.
